questions.q: In what year was Temujin formally proclaimed Genghis Khan at the quriltai, and what does the title "Genghis Khan" literally mean?
questions.a: 1206; "Universal Ruler" or "Oceanic Ruler" (from Mongolian *chinggis* = ocean/universal, *khan* = ruler). A wrong answer (e.g., 1204 or "Great Khan") reveals confusion between the Naiman defeat and the formal proclamation, or conflation with the later title "Great Khan" used by successors.

questions.q: Why did Temujin's alliance with Toghrul (Wang Khan) of the Kereyids collapse, and how did this betrayal reshape Temujin's political strategy?
questions.a: Toghrul, pressured by his son Senggum and Jamukha, attempted to assassinate Temujin at a feast (c. 1203). Temujin escaped, regrouped at Baljuna, and swore the "Baljuna Covenant" with loyal followers—binding them by oath, not kinship. This shifted his base from tribal patronage to personal loyalty, enabling recruitment across clan lines. A wrong answer focusing only on "jealousy" misses the structural shift from kinship to covenant-based loyalty.

questions.q: Compare Temujin's treatment of defeated aristocrats (e.g., the Tatar and Naiman nobility) with his treatment of common soldiers. What does this reveal about his state-building strategy?
questions.a: He executed rival aristocrats (Tatar chiefs, Naiman leaders) to eliminate alternative power centres, but absorbed common soldiers into his decimal units (mingghan, tumen) regardless of clan origin. This reveals a deliberate strategy: decapitate tribal leadership while co-opting the military manpower, replacing vertical clan loyalty with horizontal imperial loyalty. A wrong answer claiming "he killed everyone" or "he spared everyone" misses the calibrated political logic.

questions.q: Analyse the significance of the Baljuna Covenant (c. 1203) as a turning point in Temujin's rise. How did it function as a proto-constitutional moment?
questions.a: At Baljuna, Temujin swore an oath with 19 companions (Muslims, Buddhists, Christians, shamans) sharing meagre resources, pledging mutual loyalty unto death. It created a trans-ethnic, trans-religious brotherhood based on personal commitment—a "social contract" preceding the 1206 quriltai. This allowed him to recruit beyond his Borjigin clan. A wrong answer treating it as merely a "survival story" misses its role in legitimising a new political community.

questions.q: Evaluate the claim: "Genghis Khan's unification of the Mongols was primarily a military achievement." Use evidence from the 1206 quriltai reforms to support or refute.
questions.a: Refute. The 1206 quriltai instituted: (1) decimal military-civil administration (arban, jagun, mingghan, tumen) merging civil and military roles; (2) the *keshig* (imperial guard) as a meritocratic corps binding elite families to the centre; (3) the Yasa as a supra-tribal law code; (4) redistribution of booty to weaken clan hoarding. These were political-institutional innovations, not just battlefield victories. A wrong answer focusing only on battles ignores the constitutional restructuring at 1206.

questions.q: Construct a historical argument: "The 1206 quriltai was the Mongol equivalent of a constitutional convention." Identify three specific reforms enacted there that support this analogy, and one limitation of the comparison.
questions.a: Three reforms: (1) Decimal reorganisation dissolving tribal units into mixed-arbitrary units; (2) Yasa promulgation establishing rule of law above khan's whim (theoretically); (3) *Keshig* creation institutionalising succession and elite integration. Limitation: No separation of powers—khan remained legislator, executor, judge; the "constitution" was oral and revocable. A poor answer lists military wins or misses the institutional novelty of 1206.
